name: Focal Palmoplantar and Gingival Keratoderma
aliases: Focal Palmoplantar Keratoderma with Gingival Involvement

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Focal Palmoplantar and Gingival Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of well-demarcated hyperkeratotic plaques localized to the palms and/or soles
Hyperkeratotic lesions involving the gingival mucosa
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperplasia with orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both focal palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and gingival keratoderma lesions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may assist but is not always definitive; diagnosis primarily clinical and histopathological.

laboratory: Histopathology showing epidermal hyperplasia with orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis
Negative fungal cultures to exclude tinea infections
genetic: Possible mutations in keratin genes (e.g., KRT1, KRT9) associated with palmoplantar keratodermas
other: Clinical examination revealing sharply demarcated keratotic plaques on palms, soles, and gingiva

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse rather than focal involvement of palms and soles
Presence of severe periodontitis with early tooth loss
Associated palmoplantar keratoderma with systemic infections

redFlags: Rapid progression of keratoderma with ulceration
Severe gingival inflammation with tooth mobility
Signs of secondary infection such as purulence or systemic symptoms
references: Orphanet: Focal Palmoplantar and Gingival Keratoderma - ORPHA:2200
Fischer J, et al. Palmoplantar keratodermas: clinical and molecular classification. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2000.
Rajpopat S, et al. The genetic basis of palmoplantar keratoderma. Br J Dermatol. 2013.
